mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the founder's country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD and UBO piercing under Ley 23/2015 and RBF rules; screening of all Foundation Council members, protectors, and ultimate beneficial owners against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists, Panama's UAF designated-person lists, and FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions / NCCT statements. Threshold set at 25% ownership or control interest. Enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth, and source-of-funds evidence are triggered for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictional exposure, or adverse sanctions hits. Records must be retained for at least five years after the relationship terminates.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Servicios en Línea / Sede Electrónica, entity-type selector 'Fundación de Interés Privado' (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name must be expressed in Latin script; Spanish or English names are standard, and non-Latin-script brands must be transliterated into an approved Latin-script version. The complete name must be distinctive and not misleading, must not imitate existing registered entities, must not include corporate suffixes reserved for 'S.A.', 'Inc.', 'LLC' or 'Ltd.', and should terminate with 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' (or an approvable abbreviation) to identify the juridical form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms that falsely imply state sponsorship, public authority, or regulated financial services
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The initial 30-calendar-day name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 calendar days upon payment of the renewal tariff and submission of evidence that formation steps are actively being completed. If the Public Registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant's Panamanian attorney may file a reconsideration request with the Director General of the Registro Público within five (5) business days from notification. A further administrative-litigation appeal lies before the Sala Tercera (Administrative Litigation Chamber) of the Corte Suprema de Justicia. In parallel, a modified alternative name may be reserved and refiled without waiting for the appeal to be resolved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted for a non-licensed email-infrastructure SaaS business: the Private Interest Foundation must maintain a physical registered seat in Panama through a licensed foundation agent / resident agent with capacity to receive service of process. A purely virtual mailing address without local Panamanian representation is not acceptable. The actual API hosting, server location, and personnel may lawfully remain outside Panama.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: annual probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection estimated at 0–5% for an unlicensed, low-risk data-processing and newsletter-infrastructure entity. Inspections would generally be triggered only by a suspicious-transaction report, law-enforcement request, judicial order, administrative complaint, or targeted sectoral risk audit by the UAF or Registro Público.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law 13 of 2008; Articles 1–26 (creation, endowment, registration, council autonomy, and dissolution)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) – Legal Persons Section (Sección de Personas Jurídicas)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado), executed before a Panamanian Notary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Absolute minimum initial endowment of US$10,000, payable in cash, promissory instruments, or assets; must be deposited into a Panamanian bank account in the foundation’s name prior to or within 30 days of registration, with deposit evidence retained by the Registered Agent
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the Founder’s initial endowment of US$10,000 is unconditionally contributed to the Foundation’s patrimony and acknowledged as fully paid; (2) that the administrative office located at Avenida Balboa, Edif. Ocean Business Plaza, Panama City, is adopted as the Foundation’s registered office and the designated Resident Agent is confirmed in office; (3) that Council Member individuals are appointed as Foundation Council with joint administration authority; (4) that the Council is authorized to open corporate bank accounts, sign commercial instruments, and engage the email infrastructure service provider; and (5) that the Subscriber and Council are instructed to effect the Public Registry filing and municipal registration without further ratification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Online Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name request via the online platform; ensure the proposed foundation name ends in 'Fundación' and does not conflict with existing entities; upon approval, pay reservation fees and obtain a name reservation certificate with 30-day validity.
required_dossiers: Application form for name reservation
Copy of applicant identification (passport or corporate ID)
Proposed foundation name (three alternatives)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, re-file with a distinctive designation or request administrative review within 3 business days; no penalty applies on first refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter incorporating the standard articles required by Law 25 (name, registered office, endowment, foundation council, council members, beneficiary, PEF clauses, dissolution rules). Execute before a Panama Notary Public. If real property is included, the charter must be raised by notarial protocol and registered with the Public Registry.
required_dossiers: Name reservation certificate
Memorandum of charter (Spanish language)
Photocopies of Founder(s) and Council Members' passports
Evidence of Registered Agent acceptance
Certificate of good standing if founder is a legal entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires amendments, execute a corrective addendum and re-submit; administrative re-sealing is not required unless the charter affects registered immovable property.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Public Registry filing and fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Legal Persons Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the notarial instrument and required copies to the Registry’s Legal Persons Section; pay stamp tax and filing fees; the Foundation acquires legal personality upon the Registry’s inscription; obtain the 'Inscripción' certificate and certified copy of the charter.
required_dossiers: Notarial copy of Foundation Charter
Original name reservation
Proof of payment of registry fees
Registry forms (Form 6258 or successor form)
Settlement of municipal and fiscal stamps
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registry queries (notas) must be answered within 5 business days by filing corrected copies or clarifications; appeals can be lodged with the Director of the Public Registry within 3 days of the query date. Failure to respond leads to abandonment, requiring a fresh filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After Registry inscription, file DGI Form 402-RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) with the foundation charter and registered address; obtain the RUC number and taxpayer certificate; apply for the monthly informational return regime and, if applicable, electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) enrollment.
required_dossiers: Certified foundation charter and Registry inscription
Registered Agent letter appointing the tax address
Founder and Council Members identification
DGI Form 402-RUC and addendum 1 (tax domicile)
Bank account reference letter (if available)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If documentary deficiencies are noted, cure by submitting the missing original documents to the DGI window within 10 business days; administrative reconsideration is available under the Tax Code.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the municipal 'Aviso de Operación' with the Dirección de Rentas Municipales using the RUC and foundation charter; classify the activity under ISIC 6201 (high-tech software services, no physical industrial plant); obtain the municipal assessment and operating permit card.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate and tax residence proof
Foundation charter certification
Certified copy of Registry inscription
Lease agreement for registered office, plus notarized landlord consent
Completed municipal application form and local fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal rejections are resolved by correcting declaratory data (e.g., exact address or activity classification) and re-submitting; protests lie to the Municipal Mayor within 5 days of the denial decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and endowment deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banking institution (e.g., Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá licensed bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Foundation charter, Registry inscription, RUC, municipal permit, and tax domicile to the bank's legal compliance unit. The foundation must deposit the US$10,000 minimum endowment either before registration (escrow account) or within 30 days post-registration, evidenced by a bank certificate issued to the Resident Agent.
required_dossiers: Foundation Charter and Registry inscription (certified copies)
RUC and municipal aviso de operación
Resolution of Foundation Council appointing named authorized signatories
Bank account application forms and beneficial ownership declarations
Reference letters and any additional compliance due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank submits doubts under know-your-customer protocols, supply additional source-of-funds evidence within 7 business days; if account opening is ultimately denied by that bank, select a second licensed bank and comply with its enhanced due diligence requests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Dirección General de Industrias, Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – pure digital service / software hosting activity; no manufacturing or industrial operating permit required

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – National Environmental Evaluation Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Registration (Informe de TaskScreening / Ficha de Evaluación Ambiental), limited to low-impact office-based computer service activities; no full Environmental Impact Study required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office waste handling per Resolution No. PE-RN-2017, Annex III; no process wastewater or air pollutants generated; electronic waste disk-recycling obligation under Law No. 8 of 2018 (e-waste) and its 2021 regulation; compliance with MiAMBIENTE waste report if leased premises exceeds 500 m² of floor area

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (Visto Bueno) from the Dirección General de Bomberos de Panamá obtained by inspecting the registered office; structural load inspection by the Municipal Engineering Directorate (Dirección de Ingeniería Municipal) for the office floor load limit (max 250 kg/m²) of server and UPS equipment; workplace environment and occupational hazard clearance from the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) under Resolution 2020-408; no industrial civil defense license applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; operational online portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa); electronic invoicing platform operated through the same DGI web services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must: (1) maintain a licensed Panamanian resident agent and a registered office; (2) submit to the DGI the certified Public Registry inscription certificate (Ficha Registral) of the foundation together with the foundation charter and powers of attorney; (3) file the RUC inscription application (Formulario de Inscripción al Registro Único de Contribuyente) via the DGI portal or through a licensed Panamanian CPA; (4) obtain the RUC number and, where taxable activities are carried out, activate the ITBMS taxpayer registration; (5) obtain a DGI-recognized digital certificate (certificado digital) for mandatory electronic invoicing. The initial endowment/minimum capital requirement established in the foundation charter must be evidenced to the DGI; no separate statutory paid-in capital threshold applies to PIFs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope. The PIF is a distinct legal person classified as a non-commercial foundation for Panamanian tax purposes. Income sourced and effectively realized outside Panama is outside the Panamanian tax net; only Panamanian-source income is subject to the 25% corporate income tax (ISR) and the 7% ITBMS. The PIF is not a pass-through entity and is not subject to entity-level tax on foreign-source assets or income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama applies a territorial/source-based tax system without a US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections for a PIF include: (a) registration in the simplified Small Taxpayer Regime (Pequeño Contribuyente / Régimen Simplificado) where annual gross taxable turnover does not exceed B/.36,000; (b) the option to maintain an offshore character under the 1995 Foundation Law, with no Panamanian income tax exposure while no Panamanian-source income arises; (c) election of the accelerated ITBMS export credit refund procedure (reintegro rápido) for zero-rated exporters; and (d) election of a special tax-exempt zone regime (e.g., SEM, Zone Franca, or Panama Pacifico) when the activity qualifies. No hybrid-mismatch election or deemed dividend election exists under Panamanian domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS – Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (value-added-type transfer tax on movable goods and services)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (Balboas, approximately USD 36,000 at the fixed 1:1 parity) of annual gross taxable turnover for the simplified Pequeño Contribuyente regime; full ITBMS registration is mandatory when taxable supplies exceed this threshold or when the taxpayer opts for regular-taxpayer status. Non-resident digital services supplied into Panama may create a registration obligation where the DGI determines a Panama-source supply or a taxable local user base.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) applies in Panama; exporters, large taxpayers, and progressively all ITBMS taxpayers must issue invoices through DGI-approved channels using DGI-assigned invoice ranges and a fiscal QR/digital stamp generated by the DGI e-invoicing API. Invoices are validated in near-real-time with a PKI-based digital certificate; XML/CII structured data are transmitted to the DGI e-invoicing web service. Traditional printed 'bollo' fiscal forms are being phased out.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% ITBMS applies when merchandise is physically exported from Panama under a customs export declaration evidencing departure. Services, including the email API and newsletter hosting platform: 0% ITBMS applies when the service is rendered to a non-resident recipient and the benefit is effectively received or used abroad; cross-border digital services qualify if the client is established outside Panama and the place of consumption is foreign. The PIF must demonstrate that subscribers, users, and payment rails are foreign, and the invoice issued to the foreign client must state that it covers a zero-rated export service to a non-resident.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera/DUA or DUCA transmitted through the SIGA customs system to the DGI and National Customs Authority)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure of the goods from Panama

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) evidencing receipt of the export price through the Panamanian banking system; for services, bank statements showing settlement of Stripe/credit-card income into a Panamanian bank account
Commercial invoice and export service contract identifying the non-resident client, the Panamanian PIF exporter, and the place of consumption abroad
Supporting server/IP and user-domicile logs or customer records where relevant, plus certificate of origin if requested by the DGI
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI audits zero-rated exporters under the territorial-source and repatriation rules. Claiming 0% ITBMS without customs documentation, valid service contracts, or payment/repatriation proof is treated as illegal invoicing and abusive zero-rating. Consequences include: denial and retrospective clawback of the ITBMS credit refund; fines of 50% to 200% of the evaded tax; statutory default interest and surcharges under the Código Fiscal; possible criminal liability for tax evasion; and, where export proceeds are not brought into the Panamanian banking system within the 180-day window, reclassification of the income as Panama-source with exposure to 25% income tax, additional surcharges, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama has no independent central bank. The monetary system is fully dollarized with the United States dollar as legal tender. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) regulates all banking, foreign-exchange-adjacent, and AML/CFT activities; monetary policy is conducted essentially through U.S. dollar monetary conditions, administered regionally by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and SBP supervisory policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama imposes no exchange controls and maintains full convertibility under both capital and current account classifications. There is no central-bank exchange approval, no capital repatriation permit, and no differentiation between hard and soft currencies. Profit remittances from Panama to foreign beneficiaries are unrestricted, subject only to the tax rules of Panama's territorial taxation regime and standard SBP-mandated anti-money-laundering KYC evidence. For the offshore email newsletter and SaaS platform activity of a Private Interest Foundation (PIF), all receipts may be held, cleared, and disbursed in USD with no conversion or surrender requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation exists for export or services proceeds. Panama is not a central-bank dollar-rationing regime. Entities may retain 100% of their export/service revenue in USD. The only requirements are ordinary banking documentation, source-of-funds traceability, and suspicious-transaction reporting obligations under SBP AML/CFT regulations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD) and Settlement Account for cross-border SaaS receipts
Operational Account (USD), merchant settlement account, and liquidity concentration account
Capital Escrow Account / Reserve Account (USD) for contributed foundation capital and treasury reserves
Operational Account (USD) with digital banking and high-transaction API integration

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium only for secondary settlement channels, not as primary treasury infrastructure. Panama permits licensed fintech and payment system participants to operate within its bank-regulated framework, but offshore digital EMIs without an SBP license cannot clear into Panama's local USD settlement network. Offshore EMIs or neobanks holding European or other foreign licenses are not recognized as local banks in Panama and may create correspondent-bank derisking, prohibited payment service exposure, and card-scheme non-compliance. An SBP-regulated bank, or a Panamanian bank's licensed digital banking arm, must be used as the governed clearing endpoint for Stripe Billing, credit card, and API-related settlement flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Panama banks require at least one physical in-country onboarding step for the appointed foundation council president or a senior signatory. Remote account opening is possible only in narrowly tailored private-banking arrangements after a completed high-touch KYC pre-clearance, but the enforceable minimum for a Private Interest Foundation is hybrid onboarding: submission of notarized and certified foundation documents, certified identification for all signatories, a physically attended interview with an authorized representative in Panama, and verification of the registered agent. Failure to comply with physical presence is a predictable account-rejection and OFAC-friction event.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation with a non-transparent beneficial ownership chain, possible nominee foundation council members, or unclear founder control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter and Foundation Bylaws with Public Registry of Panama sealed registration; complete register of the initial foundation council; notarized beneficial-ownership statement listing every natural-person founder and ultimate beneficiary; SBP-compliant corporate due-diligence questionnaire; registered agent acceptance letter; certified subsisting certificate from the Public Registry; foundation council resolution designating opening signatories and treasury authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity transactional SaaS revenue from bulk email newsletter and API infrastructure, with low average ticket sizes and recurring cross-border counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan for the email API and newsletter hosting platform; product terms and subscriber agreements; Stripe merchant settlements and billing history; complete historical bank statements showing source of funds; internal P&L or accountant-prepared financial statements; transaction registers for trailing 12 months; network diagrams explaining customer payment flows, API usage, and email delivery contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Territorial tax optimization and minimal Panamanian economic substance; no physical office or local employees
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office and registered agent evidence in Panama; foundation council minutes approving the offshore email SaaS business plan and banking arrangement; substance dossier showing invoicing, contractual management, supplier selection, and customer correspondence from Panama; tax-residence explanation under Panama's territorial tax code; transfer-pricing documentation if related-party service fees are involved; annual internal financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Global payment-network exposure in higher-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned-country subscriber traffic, or excessive card chargeback risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative sanctions hits against OFAC, UN, UK, and EU lists for all founders, beneficial owners, signatories, and key customers; IP and geolocation blocking of prohibited countries; automated AML/sanctions screening outputs from the payment processor; sanctions-compliance policy; chargeback mitigation policy; enhanced due-diligence file for any customer identified as high risk; incident-response and blocked-person handling procedures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from founders or external investors must be routed through international USD wire rails, principally SWIFT MT103 or U.S. Fedwire, with the PIF's exact legal name, Public Registry foundation certificate number, and beneficiary account number included in the payment message. The wire purpose field should unambiguously read 'Capital contribution to Panama Private Interest Foundation' or 'Subscription of foundation assets'. Panama imposes no central-bank filing or exchange-control preapproval, but the receiving SBP-regulated bank will require a concurrent submission package: foundation capital subscription instrument, foundation council resolution approving the contribution, source-of-funds evidence for each remitter, passport copies and certified corporate records of the contributing entity, and the PIF's bank account application. Where a non-resident corporate shareholder or funding company is involved, include its certificate of good standing, directors register, UBO declaration, and audited financial statements to avoid correspondent-bank return.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational disbursements to overseas vendors and infrastructure suppliers, the clearing protocol prioritizes (i) SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers through a Panama tier-1 bank, using the full U.S.-dollar correspondent clearing footprint of CHIPS or Fedwire; (ii) local USD clearing through Panama's automated clearinghouse for domestic subscription payments and payroll; (iii) commercial letters of credit only for high-value hardware or data-center procurement when contractually required, with standard UCP600 terms; and (iv) card-scheme payouts routed through Stripe's acquiring bank into the PIF's Panama treasury account via merchant-payout MT103 or automated settlement file. All transfers must include a precise purpose narrative, standard description 'email SaaS subscription / API infrastructure disbursement', and the ultimate beneficiary's legal name. PCI DSS requirements must be preserved because card settlement data flows through Stripe and the Panama bank. For any counterparty in an OFAC-watch country or high-risk industry, an enhanced due-diligence memo and balance attestation must be attached to the treasury file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable U.S. dollar foreign-exchange forward contracts with Panama tier-1 banks or their international correspondents against USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/COP, USD/MXN, and USD/BRL to hedge any non-USD revenue or operating expenses, subject to an approved foundation council treasury policy.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through U.S. or international counterparty desks for restricted or non-clearing currencies such as USD/CNY, USD/ARS, and other manageability-constrained emerging-market currencies, with risk mitigation limits and a prohibition on speculative trading.

Cross-currency swaps for long-dated infrastructure or acquired-company liabilities, documented with a formal hedge rationale and foundation council authorization, provided no leverage or speculative output is created and all derivative transactions are recorded in the PIF's books.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Single Tax (Tasa Única Anual) for Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público) via licensed resident agent; paid through Banco Nacional de Panamá/DGI collection channels
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, on or before 31 January of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge, interest, and temporary suspension of the foundation's registry standing; prolonged non-payment can lead to administrative strike-off after not less than 90 days' notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Between 1 March and 31 March of the year immediately following the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine under Panama's Tax Code (up to USD 10,000), interest on any unpaid tax, and risk of tax registry exclusion if unresponsive.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Sworn Declaration of Final Beneficiaries (Declaración de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during July, or as designated by DGI's last-digit RUC polling calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties under Law 116 of 2019 (substantial fines per month of delay and potential public-registry suspension until filing is regularized).

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No audit is compulsory for a non-trading Private Interest Foundation; an audit becomes mandatory if the foundation performs Panama-source commercial activity and gross annual Panama-source income exceeds B/. 250,000 (USD 250,000), or if the foundation agreement/beneficiaries require an annual independent audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS/NIIF as adopted in Panama; a non-commercial PIF may keep internal books under IFRS or internationally accepted accounting principles, with no statutory publication or filing obligation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual beneficial-ownership renewal must be filed with the DGI during the July filing period. Changes in foundation council membership, ownership/beneficiary rights, or shareholding transfers must be recorded in the statutory registers and reported electronically within 30 days of the transaction; the annual confirmation reconciles all recorded transfers with the current beneficial ownership schedule.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 – USD 2,500 when an audit is triggered

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard Corporate Income Tax on Panamanian-source income under the territoriality principle, Article 694 of the Tax Code)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-source income excluded from the tax base when all operative activity occurs outside Panama; small-taxpayer regime (ISB) with graduated 0%-15% rates for gross income up to B/.200,000 and net taxable income of B/.200,000 or less; dividends from taxed profits bear 10% complementary tax; no wealth/net worth tax; capital gains on shares in Panamanian companies taxed at 10% if subject to the special regime or at 25% if not.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 105 (Declaración Anual de Renta) - Annual Corporate Income Tax Return filed through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) e-Tax 2.0 electronic portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registro Único de Contribuyentes number, full legal name of the Private Interest Foundation (PIF), resident agent details, fiscal period covered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial owners must not appear as taxpayers; the Panamanian Resident Agent's data and the PIF's foundation registration number must be quoted exactly.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenues derived from the email newsletter infrastructure platform (subscription fees, API usage charges, Stripe_Billing card settlements), classified as Panamanian-source or foreign-source.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-source revenue only if the service is rendered entirely outside Panama. Digital newsletter and bulk-email services consumed by clients located in Panama are deemed Panamanian-source under Executive Decree 452 of 2020; attach customer jurisdiction schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs directly attributable to earning Panamanian-source taxable income: hosting fees, staff payroll, resident agent fees, software amortization, bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No deduction for expenses attributable to foreign-source income; intercompany charges require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and are allowed only at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profits computed under Tax Code Articles 694-762 after statutory deductions, amortization and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the five-year loss carryforward only against Panamanian-source profits; losses from foreign-source operations may not be offset.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% standard rate, or ISB graduated bands where the small-taxpayer criterion is satisfied; any complementary tax adjustments are recorded as a separate account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure the PIF's settlement is fully funded from its own USD/B/. bank account before filing; underpayment triggers the 10% complementary dividend tax account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 36 - Payments on Account and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for Form 106 quarterly advance payments, withholding tax certificates, and any admissible foreign tax credits attributable to Panama-source operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile against funds remitted from payment rails and payment processors; retain the electronic payment vouchers for DGI audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net corporate income tax due or refund claim after crediting prepayments and withholdings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Balance must be paid by 31 March via e-Tax online banking; refund claims require certified financial statements under which independent audits may be requested.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fine of 5% of the tax due (minimum B/.25), 1% monthly default interest, automatic DGI collection and embargo of bank accounts; false filing of the annual return exposes the PIF to evasion penalties and criminal prosecution (2-5 years imprisonment).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 106 (Declaración de Pago de Anticipos del Impuesto sobre la Renta) - Quarterly Advance Corporate Income Tax Payment filed through DGI e-Tax 2.0.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Each instalment equals 25% of the prior year's final income tax liability and is payable during the months of April, July, October and December of the running fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Designation of the quarter covered (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4) and the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A zero-advance filing is required for newly incorporated PIFs without a prior-year assessed tax; a return must still be submitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of income tax determined in the immediately preceding fiscal year's Form 105 (Line 29).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Redetermination using expected current-year profit is allowed only where the taxpayer demonstrates a permanent decline in Panamanian-source activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 25% of the prepayment base per quarter.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Instalments must be funded from the PIF's corporate bank account; offsetting against accounts receivable is not permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic receipt number issued by e-Tax 2.0 after settlement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain all vouchers for credit reconciliation in the Form 105 annual filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Missed or late prepayment: monthly 1% surcharge, automatic interest capitalization and immediate enforcement proceedings; continuous non-payment authorizes DGI to issue travel bans on the foundation council and attach bank deposits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 910 (Declaración Informativa de Precios de Transferencia) - Annual Transfer Pricing Information Statement filed through DGI e-Tax 2.0.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due concurrently with Form 105 (within three months after fiscal year-end, i.e., 31 March for calendar-year filers) only when the statutory transfer pricing threshold is exceeded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, tax identification, jurisdiction and relationship code for every related party with which the PIF transacted during the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the ultimate beneficial owner's entities and any affiliated group platforms in the same corporate tree; transactions with entities domiciled in tax havens or preferential regimes must be flagged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregated value of related-party transactions by category: software licensing, hosting services, marketing, technical support, IP royalties and intercompany financing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bulk email API licensing and newsletter infrastructure fees must be priced against third-party comparator transactions; submit a functional and risk analysis for the SaaS platform.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of the most appropriate OECD-aligned methodology for each transaction class: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM or Profit Split.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For platform licensing to foreign affiliates, the DGI expects CUP or TNMM with a documented benchmarking study; profit split is accepted only for complex integrated operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the Local File (transfer pricing study) and Master File have been prepared and are available in Panama for DGI inspection.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Files must be physically or electronically retrievable in Panama within 45 days of demand; certify only if a complete benchmarking study exists.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-filing or materially incorrect Form 910: administrative fine of B/.10,000-B/.50,000; DGI recharacterization of intercompany pricing with a 30% surcharge on the omitted tax, 1% monthly interest and, in fraudulent cases, criminal liability for false declarations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% complementary dividend tax (impuesto complementario) on dividends paid out of Panamanian-taxed profits (Tax Code Article 733); 20% final distribution tax on dividends paid out of untaxed or exempt profits unless the PIF elects to pay the 10% catch-up complementary tax on such profits, in which case the 20% distribution tax is waived.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's treaty network includes Mexico, Spain, the United Kingdom, Ireland, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, Singapore, South Korea, the UAE, Barbados, Qatar, Luxembourg and others. Process: (1) obtain a Panamanian Tax Residency Certificate ('Certificado de Residencia Fiscal') from the DGI; (2) file the DGI treaty-relief application with the foreign parent's Tax Residency Certificate issued by the contracting state, a beneficial-ownership declaration and evidence that the recipient has no permanent establishment in Panama; (3) obtain the DGI's administrative authorization addressed to the paying entity to apply the reduced rate; (4) apply the reduced rate prospectively and, where over-withheld, file a refund claim within the statute of limitations window.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory 12.5% withholding tax on interest and IP royalties paid to non-residents; treaty rates generally reduce to 5%-10% for beneficial owners (e.g., Mexico Convention: 10% interest, 10% royalties; UK, Spain, Netherlands and Italian Conventions similarly provide reductions). Panama-source characterization of software royalties depends on the place of exploitation of the IP; cross-border licensing agreements must be reported consistently on Forms 105 and 910.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panamanian balboa (B/.) threshold: taxpayers with annual consolidated gross revenue equal to or above B/.10 million must file Form 910 and prepare Local and Master Files; taxpayers falling below B/.10 million are still required to prepare contemporaneous local documentation when related-party transactions exceed B/.2.5 million per counterparty or when a counterparty is resident in a low-tax or preferential regime.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Law 254 of 2021 and Executive Decree 105 of 2022 apply the Economic Substance Regulations to PIFs engaged in relevant activities. The email-newsletter infrastructure platform, software licensing and IP holding constitute relevant activities and the PIF must demonstrate in Panama: (i) core income-generating activities performed locally (development, hosting oversight, client support, contract management); (ii) adequate physical premises and full-time employees in Panama; (iii) sufficient local operating expenditure commensurate with the income; and (iv) board or foundation council meetings held in Panama. A pure equity-holding PIF benefits from reduced substance requirements but must still file the annual Economic Substance Declaration with the DGI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing Form 105 that falsely excludes foreign newsletter-infrastructure revenue as exempt without proof that all operational activities occurred outside Panama; understating Stripe_Billing settlements or credit-card receivables; fabricating deductible expenses or shell-vendor invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penal Code Article 284 and Tax Code Article 761-A: imprisonment of 2-5 years, criminal fines, civil penalty of up to 100% of the evaded tax, plus monthly 1% default interest and the nullity of the fraudulent return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation council members and signatories are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt when false returns were signed or corporate funds were diverted; criminal arrest, DGI travel ban (inhibición de salida del país), asset embargo and disqualification from acting as directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A PIF holding the software platform and collecting newsletter infrastructure income while having no physical office, no employees, no board meetings in Panama and no substance records; filing a false Economic Substance Declaration subsequent to Law 254 of 2021.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines of up to B/.1,000,000 per infraction; cancellation of the Panamanian tax residence certificate; recharacterization of income as taxable in the beneficiary jurisdiction; the PIF's separate legal personality may be disregarded as a mere facade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Members of the Foundation Council and the Resident Agent face personal fines; repeated or wilful false declarations expose them to imprisonment for false testimony before the DGI and to travel restrictions pending resolution of substance audits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering and False Beneficial Ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the PIF and the email-marketing platform to layer or disguise criminal proceeds, concealing the identity of ultimate beneficial owners from the Registro de Transparencia (UBO registry), or processing payments through undisclosed shell payment-processing accounts under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to B/.1,000,000 imposed by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF); freezing and confiscation of accounts; money-laundering offences carry 5-12 years of imprisonment; the PIF's foundation charter may be cancelled.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, ultimate beneficial owners and the Resident Agent incur joint criminal and civil liability; courts pierce the corporate veil where the PIF has no substance; travel bans, preventive detention and international asset-seizure orders are routinely granted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Licensing the email API and newsletter software to affiliated entities at prices outside the arm's length range; failing to file Form 910 once the B/.10 million revenue threshold is exceeded; refusing to produce Local and Master Files; using artificial profit-split allocations to shift profits abroad.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI adjustment of taxable income to the arm's length result; 30% surcharge on the omitted tax; 1% monthly interest; fines of B/.10,000-B/.50,000 for missing Form 910; automatic extension of the statute of limitations while documentation remains outstanding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who certified a false Form 910 face fines and imprisonment (2-5 years); parent-group directors may be held personally liable for the tax differential on intercompany pricing; travel bans and embargoes apply during the assessment phase.
